title: Quarrels at the Council's birth
summary: Why the early Traditions found unity hard.

claims.text: The founding Council drew strong-willed mages from across the known world, and infighting came with them.
The forerunners of the Dreamspeakers found the Council's European outlook ugly, the Verbena still smarted from Celestial Chorus attacks, and the Akashics thought the West undisciplined.

title: Where Avatars come from
summary: Competing beliefs about the source of a mage's power.

claims.text: Mages hold many views on the origin of Avatars, but nearly all trace them to some divine source and agree that without them there is no magic.
A Celestial Chorus view holds that the breath of life given to Adam was an Avatar from which all others descend.
Those who believe Nephandi Avatars are corrupted liken them to fallen angels.

title: Letting go of foci
summary: A step on the road past a single paradigm.

claims.text: Wisdom among mages begins when one finds that a spell no longer needs its usual focus, though the focus still makes the working easier.
Some Archmages could reach the insight of an Oracle but refuse to give up their ideas of magic, perhaps fearing they will lose power.

title: Paradox spirits and Unbelief
summary: Two dangers that weigh on flashy magic.

claims.text: Paradox spirits range from petty pests to legends such as Wrinkle, said to make overly flashy mages never have existed; most are best calmed by means other than magic.
Unbelief is the idea that things too fantastic to be accepted slowly fade: marvelous machines stop working, wondrous beasts die, and some fear mages themselves will follow.
